basics.name: John Otwell
basics.label: Software Engineer
basics.summary: I'm a generalist software engineer fluent with generative AI — using it to complement my own work, and building with it to complement the work of technical teams. I'm comfortable across many layers of abstraction, from data-oriented systems work to distributed infrastructure. Experience spanning biology, education, finance, cryptocurrency, and AI keeps my skillset broad and makes cross-domain learning fast.

references.name: AJ Smith
references.reference: John is a very intelligent engineer with a real passion for AI. He stays on top of the latest research and architectures, and he's hands-on: he builds on new papers himself rather than just reading about them. As a founding engineer on one of S&P Global's first commercial AI chatbots, he put that curiosity to work building a product used by real customers.

references.name: Kevin M.
references.reference: John is a strong developing software engineer who constantly engages himself in learning new things, spanning topics from blockchain engineering to the English language, and he actively forays into many other diverse branches of knowledge. John demonstrated grit and a deep ownership of his work when it came to taking action and pushing forward initiatives, actively managing tech debt, and producing specification documents, to name just a few. One thing that especially stood out to me about John is his proactive mindset designing features that are often as future-proof as possible, allowing for flexibility even as product requirements change.  John has a bright future as a technology polyglot and I believe any team would be lucky to have someone of his diverse skillset.

projects.name: Market Intelligence Chat Assistant
projects.description: Customer-facing conversational assistant over S&P Global Market Intelligence institutional ownership data
highlights: Built customer-facing chat assistant giving Investor Relations Officers natural-language access to institutional equity ownership, investor profiles, and expected-activity signals
Implemented planner-driven tool orchestration with Semantic Kernel, exposing product APIs as tools the assistant calls to answer data questions
Built retrieval-augmented (RAG) pipeline over product documentation to ground responses and answer product-usage questions alongside data queries
Delivered on Azure OpenAI as an IC on a 3-5 engineer team with QA and product ownership

projects.name: Natural-Language Query Engine
projects.description: Vanilla-Python engine translating sell-side analysts' plain-English questions into OpenSearch and SQL queries over Capital IQ sell-side data
highlights: Built a natural-language query engine over most of the sell-side data Capital IQ exposes, on a two-tier architecture: canonical relational store digested into OpenSearch indexes
Compiled plain-English questions into structured OpenSearch queries — Query DSL filters, lexical full-text matching, and aggregations
Generated SQL SELECTs against the canonical relational store for relational slices of the data
Implemented LLM-driven query generation in vanilla Python with no agent framework, shaping behavior through iterated prompt refinement
Kept the query surface read-only, generating only read queries against the derived search tier and the canonical store

projects.name: Multi-Agent Assistant Orchestrator
projects.description: Planner-led multi-agent orchestrator (LangChain/LangGraph) built as the agentic successor to the Market Intelligence chat assistant, designed to plug into multiple MCP servers
highlights: Built the agentic successor to the chat assistant: a planner-led multi-agent orchestrator, shipped to production for the Investor Relations audience
Orchestrated multiple agents with distinct tools, prompts, RAG resources, and security models using LangChain and LangGraph
Designed the tool layer to plug into multiple MCP servers, decoupling agents from any single tool source
Iterated models, prompts, and tools across agents, deploying them through Amazon Bedrock's model-serving APIs
Delivered as an IC on a 3-5 engineer team with QA and product ownership

projects.name: Market Data MCP Server
projects.description: FastMCP server uniting backend market-data APIs behind a single tool surface for AI applications and developer agent harnesses
highlights: Led the design and build of an MCP server on FastMCP, uniting backend product APIs into a single tool surface on a 3-5 engineer team
Auto-generated tool definitions from OpenAPI/Swagger specs using a little-documented FastMCP capability, replacing hand-written tool scaffolding
Built tools that queried backend APIs directly and performed cross-API data processing when single calls were insufficient
Exposed the server over both stdio and Streamable HTTP
Served two client populations in production: the multi-agent orchestrator as its primary consumer, and developers' agent harnesses across the organization as a shared tool layer
